standard_prerequisites.name: Left resolutions by free modules, flatness of a last cokernel and the flat up and down lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Derived Categories, label derived-lemma-subcategory-left-resolution (proof line 293); More on Algebra, labels more-algebra-lemma-last-one-flat (proof line 296) and more-algebra-lemma-tor-amplitude (proof line 304); Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-flat-up-down-henselization (proof line 298)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the bounded above complex of free modules representing the object, identifies a cokernel of its differentials as a flat module over the local ring, transports flatness to the strict henselization, and thereby exhibits a complex of flat modules representing the object, which is tor amplitude.

core_obligations: Collect the easy implications: the local ring maps to the henselization and to the strict henselization are faithfully flat, so tor amplitude over the strict henselization implies it over the henselization and over the local ring, and the same for the fifth case; faithful flatness also gives the equivalences relating the statements about an object defined over the local ring or over the henselization to the one over the strict henselization. It remains to prove that tor amplitude over the local ring, or over the henselization, implies it over the strict henselization (proof lines 272-285).

Prove the remaining implication: assuming tor amplitude over the local ring, the object has vanishing cohomology outside the interval, so it can be represented by a complex of free modules over the strict henselization which is zero above the upper bound; all the terms are flat over the local ring, and the cokernel of the last differential below the lower bound is a flat module over the local ring, hence by the flat up and down lemma also flat over the strict henselization (proof lines 287-300).

Conclude: the truncated complex is a complex of flat modules over the strict henselization representing the object, which by the tor amplitude criterion means that the object has tor amplitude in the interval over the strict henselization; the same argument with the local ring replaced by its henselization gives the remaining case, and the proof is complete (proof lines 300-308).
proof_roadmap: Derive all the easy implications from faithful flatness and reduce to one direction (proof lines 272-285).
Represent the object by a bounded above complex of free modules and identify a flat cokernel over the local ring (proof lines 287-298).
Transport flatness to the strict henselization and read off tor amplitude from the criterion (proof lines 300-308).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tor amplitude of an object over a local ring, over its henselization and over its strict henselization are equivalent conditions, with the expected variant when the object is pulled back from the local ring or from the henselization (statement lines 243-270, tag 0DK0). Faithful flatness disposes of the easy implications and of the descent equivalences, but the remaining direction needs a real argument: one represents the object by a bounded above complex of free modules, uses flatness over the local ring of the cokernel of the last differential below the interval, transports that flatness through the flat up and down lemma, and thereby exhibits a complex of flat modules over the strict henselization. That transport is the substance, so the claim is H2.
